definition: Software that works toward your goals on a cloud computer and through connectors, not only when you send a chat message.

tools.name: Claude Duet
tools.doorLine: Always-on agent on a cloud VM for Pro and Max.
tools.dek: Anthropic's always-on personal agent on a cloud virtual machine, included with US Claude Pro and Max during the research preview.
tools.cardLine: Morning briefs, background checks, and admin work through connectors and a cloud browser.

compare.modalities: In: text, voice messages. Out: text, files
compare.price: US Pro and Max, no extra cost in preview

parts.text: Anthropic
Research preview opened 21 Oct 2026 by waitlist. Access opens in waves; features can change during the preview.
Included in US Claude Pro and Max at no extra cost during the preview. Not on Team or Enterprise yet; Anthropic plans to bring it to those plans later. Dollar prices of Pro and Max:
Not stated by Anthropic
Claude Opus 5.5 for all work. You cannot choose a model; Duet decides how much effort a job needs.
Typed text and recorded voice messages.
Every says there is no real voice mode yet, just transcription.
Image or video in: Not stated by Anthropic.

Text messages and notifications, plus files you can review and edit: research briefs, financial models, slide decks, dashboards, and web apps. Image or video out: Not stated by Anthropic. You cannot watch or take over its browser.

Standalone app on iOS and Android, plus claude.ai. Works from its own cloud virtual machine with its own browser. Separate from the main Claude app for now. It cannot see files on your computer. Desktop app: Not stated by Anthropic.
Checks connected accounts every few hours at set intervals; morning brief once each morning.
Over 6,000 connectors and plugins in the Claude Marketplace.

Uses the plan's five-hour session and weekly limits at the same rate as chat; background checks count. One full reset of both limits on admission, usable until 30 Nov 2026. One main thread plus separate channels that share memory. Context window size, memory size, and task-count limits: Not stated by Anthropic.

capabilities.lead: What Anthropic says Duet can do during the research preview.

bullets.text: Sends a morning brief across email, calendar, and connected apps, and can start first steps such as drafting replies.
Monitors connected apps through the day and messages you only when something needs you; follows up on threads that have gone quiet.
Handles admin tasks such as scheduling meetings, unpaid invoices in QuickBooks or Stripe, payroll in Gusto, and agreements through Docusign after you approve.
Builds dashboards, forecasts, prototypes, and web apps; uses its cloud browser for sites with no connector; buys through Stripe Link or Shop Pay after approval.

strengths.lead: Where Anthropic's published design stands out against the other tools on this page.

bullets.text: Most explicit hard never list for money: no trades, no transfers between accounts, and no access to someone else's account, even with your approval.
Dedicated classifier and safety prompt for the strictest tier of sensitive information, with health and finance details only on your explicit instruction.
Largest stated connector catalogue: 6,000+.
Every called it the first personal agent they would call a pro tool, with strong channels and task list, but said email drafts are worse than Dot's.

connectors.lead: Apps and services Duet can use.

bullets.text: Uses connectors you already set up in Claude, such as Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Slack, QuickBooks, HubSpot, Docusign, and Calendly.
Supports plugins, including a small business plugin.
Partner services: Stripe, Link, and Shop Pay. Link and Shop Pay are Duet-only for now. Slack works with limits. Microsoft 365 is not available yet.

approval.lead: When Duet must stop and show you the action first.

bullets.text: Before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything, it shows you exactly what it will do and waits for approval.
If you cannot approve right away, it finishes the rest of the task and brings the approval back later.
Actions are checked by Anthropic's auto mode classifier.
Each purchase uses a one-time card, and Link asks you to approve the spend.

proactive.lead: When Duet reaches out without a fresh prompt from you.

bullets.text: Morning brief each morning; checks connected accounts every few hours and messages you only when needed.
You can tell it what to hear about and how often. Anthropic is still tuning when it messages you.
Something urgent can arrive between checks.
Carries over your Claude memory, skills, and connected apps. Channels share the same memory.
Disconnecting an app keeps memory of past info. Past-chat search can be turned off in Settings > Memory.
Searches your past Duet chats and Claude chats outside projects.
Won't trade securities, move money between accounts, or access someone else's account, even with your approval.
Doesn't make phone calls or text other people. Can read your Claude work but can't change it. Can't show its browser.
Personal errands, such as booking tickets, are weaker. Bigger tasks use more of your plan limits.

privacy.lead: How credentials and sensitive data are handled.

bullets.text: Never directly sees your passwords or sign-in tokens, following the Claude Managed Agents design.
When a site asks for a password, you type it into a separate form on your device, and the form sends it straight to the browser.
Tested by red teams and an external penetration-test firm, and covered by the public bug bounty.
Training on Duet data: Not stated by Anthropic.

comingSoon.lead: What Anthropic says is still ahead.

bullets.text: Team and Enterprise plans later.
Signing in with 1Password logins.
A richer Shopify visual editor and more safety details in the coming days.
How Duet and the main Claude app will work together is still to be decided.

sources.label: Anthropic, Introducing Claude Duet
Claude Help Center, Get started with Claude Duet
MacRumors, Anthropic Launches Claude Duet
Every, Vibe Check: Duet

updates.text: Research preview and waitlist opened for US Claude Pro and Max subscribers.

tools.name: Muse
tools.doorLine: Personal agent in a secure VM; free tier plus paid plans.
tools.dek: Meta's personal agent in an isolated cloud virtual machine, rolling out in the US with optional paid token plans.
tools.cardLine: Email, travel, forms, and long-term goals with connectors and a browser you can watch.

compare.underlyingModels: Muse Spark family (1.3 in safety post)
compare.modalities: In: text, files. Out: text, docs, images, podcasts
compare.whereRuns: iOS, Android, muse.ai, WhatsApp; secure VM
compare.price: Free tier; $20 Power; $100 Maximum per month

parts.text: Meta (Meta Superintelligence Labs). Internal code name Hatch.
Introduced 8 Sep 2026, rolling out in the US. Muse and its subscriptions are in limited testing and aren't available in all locations yet.
It is GA to the public in the US, not waitlist-gated, per press reading of anyone can use it.
A formal GA label: Not stated by Meta.

Free tier with a weekly usage limit; the free amount is Not stated by Meta. Power plan: $20/month for 500M Muse tokens per week. Maximum plan: $100/month for 3B Muse tokens per week. Subscribers must be 18+ (or age of majority) with a Meta account.
Over 900,000 downloads in the first week, per Sensor Tower.
Muse Spark family; Meta's safety post names Muse Spark 1.3.
Text messages, file uploads, and Apple Health or Android SMS connectors.
Photos of documents or meals are suggested in-app.
Voice in the phone app today: Not stated by Meta.
Text, PDFs, spreadsheets, documents, images, and podcasts.
Video generation.
You can see its browser and take over at any time.
Muse Secure VM: dedicated, isolated Linux cloud VM with Chromium. Clients: iOS, Android, muse.ai web, and inside WhatsApp. AI glasses: coming soon.
Paid plans: 500M or 3B tokens per week. Bug bounty up to $300,000. MEMORY.md file you can view. Context window size, check-in frequency, and task limits: Not stated by Meta.

bullets.text: Send email, book travel, fill out forms, and negotiate on your behalf.
Turn a long-term goal into a plan and advance it on its own; examples include selling a car, lowering a bill, or adjusting a training plan.
Turn a saved Instagram recipe reel into a grocery list; plan a dinner-party menu that respects friends' dietary needs.
Spawn subagents, build its own tools, and write custom connectors; make and edit artifacts and side chats that stay aware of the main chat.

strengths.lead: Where Meta's published design compares to the other tools here.

bullets.text: Only one of the four with a free tier, and the only one that works inside WhatsApp.
Most detailed published security design: Sentinel egress control, tainted-egress tracking, surrogate credentials, and separate privsep workers.
First AI agent covered by Link's purchase protections.
WIRED said Muse rarely seems to get lost while browsing.
Meta and third-party connectors, including Gmail, calendar, Apple Health, Android SMS, and Amazon.
Facebook, Instagram, and Threads connect automatically if they are in the same Accounts Center.
Muse can build a Custom Connector for any service with an API; Meta does not review these. Payments through Link by Stripe.
Checks with you before sensitive actions such as sending email or purchasing.
Sentinel is the sole permission authority for connector actions and all network egress; Muse cannot override it.

Approval options: Allow once, Allow for this task, Allow for this site, Always allow, Deny. Every purchase needs approval and uses a single-use card tied to one merchant, one amount, and a limited time.
Proactively helps with people's goals and suggests ideas; keeps working after you close the app and comes back when something changes.
Calendar connectors can push changes to Muse.
Has an Ideas tab, and nudged the tester the next day.
Fixed brief or check-in cadence: Not stated by Meta.
Remembers what matters to you; you can tell it to forget things or ask what it knows.
Memory may persist after you delete something. Reset deletes everything.
No toggle to turn memory off entirely.
Blocked by safety standards: harmful or illegal content, fraud and scams, actions that harm you or others, and harm to minors.
The email connector filters out one-time codes, password-reset links, and magic links.
For the full list of what it isn't built to do, Meta points to the Muse Terms. Detail: Not stated by Meta.

privacy.lead: VM data, ads, and training defaults.

bullets.text: Your data and credentials live in your VM; credentials are surrogated so the model never sees them.
Muse doesn't share your conversations or VM data with Meta ad systems; browsing can still indirectly influence the ads you see.
Training on your Muse data is on by default; you can opt out under Data controls. Meta can access VM data when necessary to support, secure, or operate the service until Confidential VM ships.
Muse Confidential VM, encrypted with a key only you hold, later this year.
AI glasses integration.
Shop Pay and 1Password connectors.

tools.name: dots
tools.doorLine: Always-on ChatGPT agent with its own cloud computer.
tools.dek: OpenAI's always-on personal agent inside ChatGPT, powered by GPT-6 Astra, with its own cloud computer and browser.
tools.cardLine: Software, creative, and ops work with plugins, optional use of your PC, and voice calls.

compare.modalities: In: text, voice, files. Out: text, docs, code, video
compare.whereRuns: ChatGPT apps, Slack, Teams; cloud PC

parts.text: OpenAI
Announced and rolling out 29 Sep 2026. Gradual rollout; access may take several days. Enterprise is a beta, off by default.

Pro users aged 18+ outside the EEA, Switzerland, and the UK; Business Premium; Enterprise, Edu, and Healthcare if an admin enables it. First dot included at no extra cost with an allowance for deeper work in the first month. Not on Plus.
Pro costs $100/month.
GPT-6 Astra for all dot work.
Text, voice calls, and file or photo attachments.
Camera, microphone, and screen only if you connect your computer and grant permission.
Text messages, documents, decks, code and pull requests, and videos showing those changes. The dot can't start a call to you. You can open its computer to inspect it or take over.
Edited video clips.

Its own cloud computer and browser. Optionally your computer through the ChatGPT desktop app (off by default). Reach it in ChatGPT desktop, web, and mobile apps, plus Slack and Teams. Not on mobile web. Texting is a limited US Pro beta.
One primary dot for now.
4,000+ apps through plugins.

Chat with the dot doesn't count toward ChatGPT limits; Codex and Work tasks do. Check-in timing: it decides when to follow up, or you set fixed schedules and event triggers. Context window size, memory size, deeper-work allowance numbers, and parallel task count: Not stated by OpenAI.

bullets.text: Turns customer feedback into tested fixes and pull requests, with videos of the changes.
Revises launch materials when scope changes; reruns analyses and updates figures for a paper.
Updates a sales proposal and builds a proof of concept; turns interview transcripts into clips, show notes, and social posts.
Starts and manages Codex cloud tasks and reads and edits ChatGPT Work automations; works on several projects at once using background agents.

strengths.lead: Where OpenAI's design differs from the other tools here.

bullets.text: Only one of the four that can work on your own computer as well as its cloud one, and the only one with voice calls to the agent.
Strongest for software and creative work through Codex integration for pull requests and tests.
Reachable in Slack and Teams.
Every said Dot's email drafts beat Duet's.
Plugins are shared with ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex.
Slack, Teams, and personal email. It can't have its own standalone email address at launch. It can have its own separate Slack account.
Specialist dots via Microsoft Agent 365 are in progress.
Custom Rules with four settings: take action without asking, take action if pre-approved, ask first, or hand off to you.
Auto-review checks actions such as email recipients and content.
Password changes and money transfers require you to take over. Merchant-saved-card purchases need approval. Asking for a draft doesn't authorise sending it.
No Stripe virtual-card checkout at review time.
Proactive research: read-only background review of connected apps; research tools can't send, change content, or control a browser.
Decides when to pause and wake.
Fixed schedules are optional, for example each weekday at 9 AM Central.
Receives ChatGPT memory and creates its own memories, including from connected apps.
You can't view or edit individual dot memories; resetting deletes them.
Its context doesn't keep credentials, images, or screenshots. Disconnecting an app doesn't delete what the dot learned from it.

limits.lead: Regional and safety limits OpenAI lists.

bullets.text: Not for under-18s; not in the EEA, Switzerland, or UK.
Some steps, such as password changes, are always yours. Custom Rules can't override core safety requirements.
Websites may block its cloud browser.
Personal plans: the Improve the model setting controls training. Business, Enterprise, and Edu: no training by default.
No direct training on proactive research or the dot's own notes. Humans may review activity for safety even when training is off.
Content is encrypted at rest and in transit.
More dots per user; scaling speed or monthly work.
Wider texting and expansion to more users soon.
Specialist dots (enterprise pilots) and Agent 365.

tools.name: Grok Bot
tools.doorLine: Named Bots on a shared cloud computer and desktop apps.
tools.dek: SpaceXAI's named Bots product with a persistent cloud computer, built with Cursor, on paid X Subscription and Cursor plans.
tools.cardLine: Parallel Bots, routines, teach-by-demo skills, and rich event triggers.

compare.underlyingModels: Routed xAI and approved third-party (incl. Opus 5.5)
compare.modalities: In: text, voice, files up to 250 MB. Out: text, decks, audio
compare.whereRuns: macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android, X @bot
compare.price: X Premium $30+; legacy Cursor paid; linked SuperGrok

parts.text: SpaceXAI (xAI), with Cursor. Docs and help live on both x.ai and cursor.com.
9to5Mac says the two firms are in the process of becoming a single company.
Beta launched 11 Aug 2026. Access expanded to more plans 21 Aug 2026.
Enterprise: generally available 3 Sep 2026. Consumer GA label: Not stated by SpaceXAI.
Included on X Subscription Premium ($30/mo), Super ($100/mo), and Ultra ($200/mo). Not on Plus ($8) or Free. Also on legacy Cursor paid plans and Teams, or by linking SuperGrok tiers.
Pricing changed quickly from $200 a month to $60 to $30 in about three days.
Routes each request to a first-party xAI model or an approved third-party model; Opus 5.5 is named as one. No model picker, and the model used isn't shown.
Type, dictate, voice chat; attachments up to 250 MB per file and 1 GB per video, 20 per message, 200 MB total.
Text, voice memos, files, Pages, slide decks, images, audio files, and PDFs of web pages.

Persistent cloud computer with browser, filesystem, and terminal in Cursor's cloud. Apps on macOS, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad, and Android. Also reachable via @bot on X. Optional local-computer execution with per-command approval by default.
Bot computer screen 1920×1200. Up to 200 plugin skills per Bot. More than 50 Bots allowed. One computer-use task per Bot screen at a time.
Unanswered approvals from background work expire after about 10 minutes. Connector calls wait up to 2 minutes. Usage resets weekly from a pool shared with Grok and Cursor.
Context window size: Not stated by SpaceXAI.

bullets.text: Runs multiple named Bots in parallel; Bots message each other in group chats and hand off tasks.
Learns a workflow from one demonstration, saves it as a skill, and reruns it on a schedule.
Routines on a schedule or triggered by Slack, GitHub, Linear, Sentry, PagerDuty, Microsoft Teams, email, or webhook events.
Bots get their own email address with +tag aliases; searches public X posts; pays with Stripe Link or X Money.

strengths.lead: Where Grok Bot's design stands out on this page.

bullets.text: Only one of the four with many Bots that coordinate in group chats, plus teach-by-demonstration.
Widest platform list: full desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux, plus iOS and Android.
Richest triggers: webhook and developer-tool events.
Ships fastest, judging by the changelog cadence.
Plugin catalogue includes Gmail, Outlook, Slack, GitHub, GitLab, Notion, Figma, Canva, Google Drive, OneDrive, 1Password, and the X plugin.
Computer use for sites without a connector. Total connector count: Not stated by SpaceXAI.
Approval cards offer Allow once, Always allow, or Deny.
Auto Review, an independent review model, checks shell commands, plugin calls, computer use, routine writes, and delegation.
Before irreversible sends, posts, buys, or deletes, it checks your own messages for approval. Enterprise admins can enforce Auto Review.
Your primary Bot will spot work it can take off your plate and offer to handle it.
Routines at any schedule you set; you pick the cadence.
Fixed default check-in: Not stated by SpaceXAI.

memory.lead: Per-Bot context on a shared computer.

bullets.text: Stable preferences, role context, and summaries of prior work, kept per Bot.
Shared files and browser sessions across Bots.
Everything on the shared computer is visible to every Bot on your account.
Hands you passwords, 2FA, CAPTCHAs, and identity checks rather than working around them.
Routines share a run-rate limit; some runs fail with Automation run rate limit exceeded.
Uses Cursor SSO and privacy mode; encrypted in transit and at rest; training opt-out.
Third-party model providers are limited to the sub-processor list.
Enterprise controls: data-loss prevention, network policy, and audit logs.
No official roadmap found: Not stated by SpaceXAI.
